questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 What are visual constraints in design?
options: They are the perceived properties of an object or interface that suggest how it can or should be used.
They are the limitations or restrictions placed on the visual elements of a design project.
They are the space of possible actions from an object's appearance, providing people with a range of usage possibilities.
They are the effective and usable elements of a design that communicate the intended message to the audience.
questions.correct_answer: They are the limitations or restrictions placed on the visual elements of a design project.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which stages did Prof. Bala Ramadurai go through to develop the four-step design thinking process of Empathize-Analyze-Solve-Test to help create better products or services?
options: Ideas → Problems → Service or Product → Test → People → Revenue
People → Problems → Service or Product → People → Test → Revenue
People → Problems → Ideas → Test → Service or Product → Revenue
People → Ideas → Test → Problems → Service or Product → Revenue
questions.correct_answer: People → Problems → Ideas → Test → Service or Product → Revenue

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Imagine you are designing the world’s first voice-guided navigation system for a car GPS. At this early stage in the design process, you want to find out if drivers can understand and respond to your voice directions while driving a car. Which prototype would you build for this purpose?
options: Have pre-determined turn-by-turn directions for a particular route written on a notepad. The experimenter reads the right directions while the participant drives on the route.

Create a fully functional system with a database of routes, directions and voice clips on a laptop and put the laptop in the car. The participant drives the car along the route and hears the turn directions from the laptop.

A paper prototype of the GPS display with multiple screens that each shows the map at a different part of a route. The participant evaluates the prototype in a lab. For each screen, the experimenter speaks out the turn directions and asks the participant what he should do (e.g., “I’d take the next exit”).
Create a video of a person driving on a route, and then add your instructions as a voiceover. Show participants this video, pause the video after each instruction and ask what participants would do.
questions.correct_answer: Have pre-determined turn-by-turn directions for a particular route written on a notepad. The experimenter reads the right directions while the participant drives on the route.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 An Agile methodology based project is about to start in a week’s time. Annabelle and Ayraa, the two developers are discussing the applicability of automation. Which of the following statements is true?

Ayraa is correct as development testing and deployment can be automated in an Agile project.
Ayraa is partially correct as deployment can’t be automated in an Agile project.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 What is the purpose of the extreme character in design thinking?

To identify the most extreme or unusual user group and design a solution that meets their needs.
To challenge assumptions and generate new ideas by considering the needs and perspectives of an extreme user group.
To exclude certain user groups from the design process in order to focus on a specific target market.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which of the following is a key difference between design research and market research?

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which of the following statements is true regarding the difference between empathy maps and journey maps?

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which of the following statements is true regarding design methods and their criticisms?

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which among the following is the correct approach to Multi-why Analysis?

Ask the customer why their problem exists, then drill down further by asking more whys till you annoy the customer
Ask the customer why their problem exists, then drill down further by asking more whys till you find out the root cause of that problem

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 What does Prof. Bala Ramadurai suggest when it comes to the application of Multi-why analysis?

CASE INCIDENT User Experience of a Grocery Store A team of IITM BS DTD-DAD students conducted in-depth interviews and observations with shoppers in the Prime Mart, a grocery store located on the IIT Madras campus, to understand their pain points and needs. They identified common issues such as long checkout lines, difficulty finding products, and confusion about pricing. The team analyzed the research findings and synthesized the information into clear problem statements. They identified the key issue as improving the checkout experience to reduce wait times and increase customer satisfaction. The team generated a variety of potential solutions through brainstorming sessions and creative exercises. They came up with ideas such as self-checkout kiosks, mobile payment options, and optimizing the layout of the store. The team created rough drafts of their ideas to test with users. They developed a mobile payment app prototype app that allowed customers to scan and pay for items as they shopped. However, they encountered some issues during the prototyping phase, such as technical glitches and difficulty integrating the app with the store’s existing systems. The team tested their prototype with real users to gather feedback and identify areas for improvement. They found that the app was well-received by users and helped to reduce checkout times, but there were still some issues that needed to be addressed before implementation.
